name: medianStream
description: Uses two heaps: a max-heap for the lower half and a min-heap for the upper half. The median is always the top of one or both heaps. After each insert, rebalance so sizes differ by at most 1.
aim: Maintain a running median of a data stream — find the median after each new number is added — in O(log n) per insert and O(1) for finding the median.
howItWorks: Lower half: max-heap (largest of smaller half at top)
Upper half: min-heap (smallest of larger half at top)
Insert: compare with maxHeap top, add to correct half
Rebalance if size difference > 1 by moving top element to other heap
Median: if equal sizes → average of two tops; else → top of larger heap

time.bestCase: Insert into heap is O(log n)
time.averageCase: Insert O(log n), find median O(1)

complexity.spaceDescription: Two heaps store all n elements

realWorld: Financial analytics: live median salary/price updates
Network monitoring: real-time median response time
Signal processing: running median filter to remove outliers
whenToUse: Need to find median after each new data point in a stream
When sorting all data each time would be too slow
alternatives: Order statistics tree: O(log n) insert + median, but complex to implement
